Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Ploidy of seed and embryo-sac tissues
solution.explanation: Perisperm is the persistent nucellus and the seed coat comes from the integuments: both are diploid maternal tissues (a). The zygote (syngamy) and nucellar cells are both diploid (b). Synergids and antipodals are cells of the haploid embryo sac (d). The endosperm is triploid while the pericarp (ovary wall) is diploid (c, different). The primary endosperm nucleus is triploid, but each polar nucleus is haploid (e, different).
steps: 2n: perisperm, seed coat, zygote, nucellus, pericarp
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) pair a triploid tissue with a diploid or haploid one.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: female gametophyte; double fertilisation; post-fertilisation: seed
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In many Citrus varieties, the development of embryos from nucellar cells that protrude into the embryo sac is a form of apomixis.
Statement II: The development of a banana fruit without fertilisation is an example of apomixis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT describes apomixis as the production of seeds without fertilisation, a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction. It names two routes: a diploid egg formed without reduction division developing into the embryo, and, more often, nucellar cells dividing and protruding into the embryo sac to form embryos, as in many Citrus and mango varieties (Statement I true). A banana fruit developing without fertilisation is parthenocarpy: a fruit, not a seed, is formed without fertilisation (Statement II false).
steps: Apomixis: seeds without fertilisation (Citrus nucellar embryos)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony; post-fertilisation: fruit
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (device) with List-II (effect).

List-I:
A. Dioecy, as in papaya
B. Unisexual flowers on a monoecious plant, as in castor
C. Self-incompatibility
D. Cleistogamy

List-II:
I. Prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy
II. Prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy
III. Inhibits pollen germination or pollen-tube growth of self-pollen in the pistil
IV. Gives assured seed set by autogamy even in the absence of pollinators

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: when male and female flowers are on different plants (dioecy, papaya), both autogamy and geitonogamy are prevented (A-II). Unisexual flowers on the same plant (castor, maize) prevent autogamy but not geitonogamy (B-I). Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen-tube growth in the pistil (C-III). Cleistogamous flowers never open, are invariably autogamous and produce assured seed set even without pollinators (D-IV).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap dioecy and monoecy, or the effects of self-incompatibility and cleistogamy, or credit monoecy with the pistil's rejection of self-pollen.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', outbreeding devices; pollination (cleistogamous flowers)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In every angiosperm seed, a persistent endosperm nourishes the embryo up to and beyond seed maturity.
Reason (R): The cells of the endosperm are filled with reserve food materials, which are used for the nutrition of the developing embryo.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: endosperm cells are filled with reserve food materials used for the nutrition of the developing embryo (R true). But the endosperm does not persist in every seed: in pea, groundnut and beans it is completely consumed by the developing embryo before seed maturation (non-albuminous seeds), and the food is stored in the cotyledons. Only in albuminous seeds such as wheat, maize, barley, castor and coconut does a part of it persist. So A is false.
steps: A: false; non-albuminous seeds lack endosperm at maturity
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: endosperm; seed
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT one of the seven characters of the garden pea that Mendel studied?

solution.explanation: NCERT's table of the contrasting traits studied by Mendel lists seven characters: stem height, flower colour, flower position, pod shape, pod colour, seed shape and seed colour. Leaf shape is not among them.
steps: Seven characters: stem height, flower colour, flower position, pod shape, pod colour, seed shape, seed colour
solution.why_others_wrong: Pod colour (green/yellow), flower position (axial/terminal) and seed shape (round/wrinkled) are all in Mendel's list.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendel's laws of inheritance (table of contrasting traits)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Leaf shape

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In his dihybrid cross, Mendel crossed a pea plant with round, yellow seeds (RRYY) with one with wrinkled, green seeds (rryy). The F1 seeds were:

options.text: Round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow and wrinkled green in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1
Round yellow and wrinkled green in the ratio 1 : 1

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the cross between round yellow and wrinkled green parents, the F1 seeds were round and yellow, because round (R) is dominant over wrinkled and yellow (Y) over green. All F1 plants are RrYy. The 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio appears only in the F2, after the F1 is self-pollinated.
steps: R and Y dominant → all round yellow
solution.why_others_wrong: 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 is the F2 ratio; wrinkled green is the recessive parental phenotype, hidden in the F1; a 1 : 1 ratio would need a heterozygous parent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes
solution.final_answer: Option C: All round and yellow

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the ABO blood group system, the allele i does not produce any sugar on the surface of red blood cells.
Statement II: The alleles Iᴬ and Iᴮ produce slightly different forms of the sugar.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the plasma membrane of red blood cells has sugar polymers protruding from its surface, and the kind of sugar is controlled by the gene I, which has three alleles, Iᴬ, Iᴮ and i. The alleles Iᴬ and Iᴮ produce a slightly different form of the sugar (Statement II true), while allele i does not produce any sugar (Statement I true).
steps: Iᴬ, Iᴮ: two forms of the sugar
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait.
Reason (R): Thalassemia is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait that can be transmitted from parents to offspring when both partners are carriers (A true). NCERT also says thalassemia differs from sickle-cell anaemia in that it is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules (R true). R describes a different disorder and says nothing about why sickle-cell anaemia is autosomal recessive, so R does not explain A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (disorder) with List-II (chromosome involved, as given in NCERT).

List-I:
A. β-Thalassemia
B. α-Thalassemia
C. Colour blindness
D. Down's syndrome

List-II:
I. Chromosome 11
II. Chromosome 16
III. X chromosome
IV. Chromosome 21

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: β-thalassemia is controlled by a single gene, HBB, on chromosome 11 of each parent (A-I); α-thalassemia by two closely linked genes, HBA1 and HBA2, on chromosome 16 of each parent (B-II). Colour blindness is sex-linked recessive, due to a mutation in certain genes on the X chromosome (C-III). Down's syndrome is caused by an additional copy of chromosome 21 (D-IV).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap chromosomes 11 and 16 between the two thalassemias, or swap the X chromosome with chromosome 21.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders; chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In NCERT's model of human skin colour controlled by three genes (A, B and C), with dominant alleles responsible for dark skin colour, how many dominant alleles does a person with the darkest skin colour carry?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the genotype with all dominant alleles (AABBCC) has the darkest skin colour and the one with all recessive alleles (aabbcc) the lightest. Three genes in a diploid give six alleles, so the darkest person carries six dominant alleles. AaBbCc, with three dominant alleles, has an intermediate skin colour.
solution.why_others_wrong: Three is the intermediate AaBbCc; one or two dominant alleles give lighter shades.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option B: Six

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A true-breeding tall pea plant (TT), on self-pollination, gives only tall progeny.
Reason (R): A homozygous parent produces two kinds of gametes in equal proportion.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in a homozygous parent all the gametes are similar, while a heterozygous parent produces two kinds of gametes, each having one allele, in equal proportion. TT forms only T gametes, so all progeny of selfing are TT and tall (A true). R is false: two kinds of gametes come only from a heterozygote.
steps: TT → only T gametes → TT progeny, all tall
Two kinds of gametes: heterozygote only → R false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: law of segregation
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant heterozygous for three independently assorting genes (AaBbCc), each with complete dominance, is test-crossed with aabbcc. How many phenotypic classes appear in the progeny, and what fraction of the progeny shows all three recessive traits?

solution.explanation: The heterozygote AaBbCc forms 2³ = 8 kinds of gametes in equal proportion (independent assortment); the aabbcc parent forms only abc. In a test cross, each gamete of the heterozygote shows up directly as a phenotype, so there are 8 classes, each 1/8. The all-recessive class (aabbcc) is 1/8.
steps: Test cross: phenotype classes = gamete kinds
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/64 is the aabbcc fraction for AaBbCc × AaBbCc, not a test cross; 27 is the number of genotypes in a trihybrid self; 4 classes and 1/4 fit a dihybrid test cross.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment; test cross
solution.final_answer: Option B: 8 classes; 1/8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Sturtevant used the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure of the distance between them. Genes A, B and C lie on one chromosome, with B between A and C. The recombination frequency is 12 per cent between A and B and 5 per cent between B and C. On this map, the distance between A and C is:

solution.explanation: Since recombination frequency is used as a measure of distance and B lies between A and C, the map distances add: A–C = A–B + B–C = 12 + 5 = 17 units.
solution.why_others_wrong: 7 subtracts the distances (correct only if C lay between A and B); 60 multiplies them; 8.5 averages them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option A: 17 units

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A woman of genotype IᴮIᴮ marries a man with blood group AB. Which blood groups are possible among their children?

solution.explanation: The woman forms only Iᴮ gametes; the man forms Iᴬ and Iᴮ gametes in equal numbers. Children are IᴬIᴮ (blood group AB, since Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant) or IᴮIᴮ (blood group B), in a 1 : 1 ratio. No child can be A or O, because every child receives Iᴮ from the mother.
solution.why_others_wrong: Group A needs no Iᴮ from the mother, which is impossible; group O needs i from both parents; 'B only' ignores the father's Iᴬ gametes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance (ABO blood groups)
solution.final_answer: Option C: B and AB only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Failure of cytokinesis after the telophase stage of cell division results in an increase in a whole set of chromosomes, a condition called polyploidy.
Statement II: Failure of segregation of chromatids during the cell division cycle results in the gain or loss of a chromosome, a condition called aneuploidy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division results in the gain or loss of a chromosome(s), called aneuploidy (Statement II true). Failure of cytokinesis after telophase results in an increase in a whole set of chromosomes in an organism, known as polyploidy, often seen in plants (Statement I true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A colour-blind man marries a woman with normal vision who is a carrier of colour blindness. Which of the following statements about their children are correct?

(a) Half of their daughters are expected to be colour blind.
(b) Half of their sons are expected to be colour blind.
(c) Every daughter will carry at least one allele for colour blindness.
(d) No son receives the allele for colour blindness from the father.
(e) None of their children will have normal vision.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Father XᶜY; mother XᶜX. Daughters get Xᶜ from the father and Xᶜ or X from the mother: half XᶜXᶜ (colour blind) and half XᶜX (carriers), so every daughter carries the allele (a, c). Sons get Y from the father and Xᶜ or X from the mother: half colour blind (b), and none gets the allele from the father (d). Normal-vision children exist (the XY sons and the carrier daughters), so (e) is false.
steps: Father's Xᶜ goes only to daughters
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) are wrong because the carrier daughters and half the sons see normally; '(b), (c) and (d)' leaves out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In NCERT's three-gene model of human skin colour, persons of genotypes AABbcc and aaBbCC have the same skin colour.
Reason (R): In polygenic inheritance the effect of each allele is additive, and both genotypes carry three dominant alleles.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in polygenic inheritance the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele, i.e. the effect of each allele is additive. AABbcc has A, A, B (three dominant alleles) and aaBbCC has B, C, C (also three). Since only the number of dominant alleles matters, the two have the same intermediate skin colour, as does AaBbCc. R gives exactly why A is true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (parents' genotypes) with List-II (probability that a child has blood group O).

List-I:
A. Iᴬi × Iᴮi
B. Iᴬi × ii
C. ii × ii
D. IᴬIᴮ × ii

List-II:
I. 0
II. 1/4
III. 1/2
IV. 1

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Blood group O needs genotype ii, i.e. an i allele from each parent. Iᴬi × Iᴮi: ½ × ½ = 1/4 (A-II). Iᴬi × ii: ½ × 1 = 1/2 (B-III). ii × ii: 1 (C-IV). IᴬIᴮ × ii: the AB parent has no i, so 0 (D-I).
steps: Multiply each parent's chance of giving i
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap 1/4 and 1/2, or give the AB × O cross a chance of O although the AB parent carries no i.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance (ABO blood groups)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In honey bees, a queen of genotype AaBb (the two genes assort independently) lays unfertilised eggs. What fraction of the drones (males) produced from these eggs is expected to be of genotype ab?

solution.concept: Drones are haploid and come from the queen's eggs
solution.explanation: NCERT: in honey bees an unfertilised egg develops as a male (drone) by parthenogenesis, so a drone is haploid and carries just the genotype of the egg. The queen (AaBb) forms four kinds of eggs, AB, Ab, aB and ab, in equal proportion. Hence 1/4 of the drones are ab.
steps: Eggs of AaBb: AB, Ab, aB, ab, each 1/4
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/16 treats drones as diploid offspring of a self-cross (aabb); 1/2 counts only one gene; 0 assumes drones need a father.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination (honey bee)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 1/4

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following comparisons are correct according to NCERT?

(a) Phenylketonuria and sickle-cell anaemia are both autosomal recessive disorders.
(b) Haemophilia and colour blindness are both sex-linked recessive disorders.
(c) Sickle-cell anaemia and thalassemia both affect the globin chains of haemoglobin.
(d) Down's syndrome and Klinefelter's syndrome are both caused by point mutations.
(e) α-Thalassemia and β-thalassemia are both controlled by genes on chromosome 11.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: phenylketonuria is an inborn error of metabolism inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, and sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait (a). Haemophilia and colour blindness are sex-linked recessive disorders (b). Sickle-cell anaemia involves a defective β-globin chain, and thalassemia a reduced synthesis of α- or β-globin (c). Down's (trisomy 21) and Klinefelter's (XXY) are chromosomal disorders from aneuploidy, not point mutations (d false). α-Thalassemia genes are on chromosome 16; only β-thalassemia's HBB is on chromosome 11 (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false comparison; '(b), (c) and (d)' also leaves out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In NCERT's three-gene model of skin colour (genes A, B and C, additive dominant alleles), how many different genotypes in total, counting AaBbCc itself, carry exactly three dominant alleles and so share its skin colour?

solution.concept: Counting genotypes with three dominant alleles
solution.explanation: AaBbCc has three dominant alleles, and with additive effects any genotype with exactly three dominant alleles has the same colour. Genotypes with three dominant alleles: one gene homozygous dominant, another heterozygous and the third homozygous recessive (AABbcc type): 3 × 2 = 6 arrangements; plus all three heterozygous (AaBbCc): 1. Total = 6 + 1 = 7.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20 is the number of the 64 F2 combinations of AaBbCc × AaBbCc that have three dominant alleles (20/64), not the number of distinct genotypes; 3 counts only one arrangement per gene (e.g. AABbcc, aaBBCc, AabbCC) and misses the rest; 1 counts only AaBbCc.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option B: 7

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A colour-blind woman married to a man with normal colour vision can have colour-blind daughters.
Reason (R): A daughter receives one X chromosome from each parent.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A daughter gets one X from her mother and one from her father (R true). A colour-blind daughter needs the recessive allele on both her X chromosomes. A father with normal vision has a normal allele on his single X, and he passes that X to every daughter; so every daughter has at least one normal allele and is a carrier with normal vision. NCERT: a daughter will normally not be colour blind unless her mother is at least a carrier and her father is colour blind. A is false.
steps: Daughters: carriers, not colour blind → A false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Parents with blood groups A and B can have children of all four blood groups, A, B, AB and O.
Statement II: Two parents who both have blood group A can have a child with blood group O.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Blood group A can be IᴬIᴬ or Iᴬi, and B can be IᴮIᴮ or Iᴮi. If the parents are Iᴬi and Iᴮi, the children can be IᴬIᴮ (AB), Iᴬi (A), Iᴮi (B) or ii (O) (Statement I true). If both A parents are Iᴬi, a quarter of their children are expected to be ii, blood group O (Statement II true).
steps: Iᴬi × Iᴮi → AB, A, B, O
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance (ABO blood groups)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A father has normal colour vision and a mother is a carrier of colour blindness (normal vision). Their daughter has Turner's syndrome (45, X0) and is colour blind. Assuming no new mutation, which explanation fits?

options.text: An egg carrying no X chromosome was fertilised by an X-bearing sperm of the father
A Y-bearing sperm fertilised an egg carrying no sex chromosome
An egg carrying the X with the colour-blindness allele was fertilised by a sperm carrying no sex chromosome
An egg carrying two X chromosomes was fertilised by a Y-bearing sperm

solution.concept: Turner's syndrome and an X-linked trait
solution.explanation: NCERT: Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes (45 with X0). With a single X, a recessive X-linked allele is expressed. The father's X carries the normal allele, so the lone X must have come from the mother and must be the one with the colour-blindness allele; the sperm contributed no sex chromosome.
steps: Colour blind → that X carries the allele
Father's X is normal → X is maternal
solution.why_others_wrong: The father's X would give a normal-vision X0 girl; a Y with no X does not give Turner's syndrome; XX + Y gives an XXY male (Klinefelter's syndrome), not a 45, X0 female.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders; colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option C: An egg carrying the X with the colour-blindness allele was fertilised by a sperm carrying no sex chromosome

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cross (genes assort independently)) with List-II (number of different genotypes among the progeny).

List-I:
A. AaBb × aabb
B. AaBB × AaBb
C. AaBb × AaBb
D. AaBbCc × AaBbCc

List-II:
I. 4
II. 6
III. 9
IV. 27

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Multiply the number of genotypes for each gene. AaBb × aabb: Aa × aa gives 2 (Aa, aa) and Bb × bb gives 2, so 4 (A-I). AaBB × AaBb: Aa × Aa gives 3 and BB × Bb gives 2 (BB, Bb), so 6 (B-II). AaBb × AaBb: 3 × 3 = 9 (C-III). AaBbCc × AaBbCc: 3³ = 27 (D-IV).
steps: Aa × aa → 2; Aa × Aa → 3; BB × Bb → 2
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes treat AaBB × AaBb as giving 4 or 9 genotypes, or swap the dihybrid (9) and trihybrid (27) counts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In Mendel's dihybrid cross RRYY × rryy, the F1 is self-pollinated. Which of the following statements about the F2 are correct?

(a) Nine different genotypes are present.
(b) Three-eighths of the F2 show combinations of traits not seen in either parent (round green or wrinkled yellow).
(c) Three-fourths of the F2 are heterozygous for at least one of the two genes.
(d) Round, green seeds form 1/16 of the F2.
(e) All the round, yellow F2 plants are of genotype RrYy.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Genotypes: 3 × 3 = 9 (a). New combinations: round green 3/16 + wrinkled yellow 3/16 = 6/16 = 3/8 (b). Homozygous at both loci: RRYY, RRyy, rrYY, rryy = 4/16, so 12/16 = 3/4 are heterozygous at one or both loci (c). Round green = 3/16, not 1/16 (d false; 1/16 is rryy). Round yellow plants include RRYY, RRYy, RrYY and RrYy, so not all are RrYy (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement; '(b), (c) and (e)' also omits (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Compare a pink-flowered snapdragon (Rr, incomplete dominance) with a person of blood group AB (IᴬIᴮ, co-dominance). Which statements are correct?

(a) In both cases, the heterozygote has a phenotype different from both homozygotes.
(b) In both cases, a cross between two such heterozygotes gives three phenotypes in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1.
(c) The pink flower is in between red and white, whereas the AB person expresses both kinds of sugar.
(d) In both cases, the two alleles blend permanently, so the parental phenotypes are never recovered.
(e) In both cases, one allele completely masks the other in the heterozygote.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Snapdragon: RR red, Rr pink, rr white; NCERT notes the F2 phenotypic ratio is 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white. ABO: IᴬIᴬ (A), IᴬIᴮ (AB), IᴮIᴮ (B), and IᴬIᴮ × IᴬIᴮ gives A : AB : B = 1 : 2 : 1. So in both, the heterozygote differs from both homozygotes (a) and the 1 : 2 : 1 ratio appears (b). The pink flower is intermediate, while co-dominant Iᴬ and Iᴮ each express their own sugar (c). Red and white (or A and B) reappear in the F2, so there is no permanent blending (d false), and neither case shows complete dominance (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) are wrong, since parental phenotypes reappear and neither allele masks the other; '(a), (c) and (d)' also omits (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: incomplete dominance; co-dominance
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: When a nucleoside is converted into a nucleotide, the phosphate group becomes attached at which carbon of its pentose sugar?

options.text: The 1' carbon, which carries the nitrogenous base

solution.explanation: NCERT: a nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of the 1' carbon of the pentose sugar through an N-glycosidic linkage to form a nucleoside. When a phosphate group is linked to the OH of the 5' carbon of the nucleoside through a phosphoester linkage, a nucleotide is formed. Two nucleotides are then joined through a 3'-5' phosphodiester linkage.
solution.why_others_wrong: The 1' carbon carries the base; the 2' carbon bears H in DNA or OH in RNA and is not the phosphate site; NCERT does not attach the phosphate at the 4' carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option D: The 5' carbon (through its OH group)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a eukaryotic nucleus, histones are organised into a unit around which the DNA is wrapped. According to NCERT, this unit consists of:

solution.explanation: NCERT: histones are organised to form a unit of eight molecules called a histone octamer. The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around this positively charged octamer to form the nucleosome, which typically contains about 200 bp of DNA helix.
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT names the unit an octamer, i.e. eight molecules, not two, four or sixteen.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option B: Eight histone molecules (a histone octamer)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the 'lac' in the name of the lac operon refers to:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the 'lac' here refers to lactose. The lac operon of E. coli consists of the regulatory i gene and the structural genes z, y and a, whose products (β-galactosidase, permease and transacetylase) are needed to take up and use the disaccharide lactose; lactose (the substrate) also acts as the inducer.
steps: Operon for lactose uptake and use
solution.why_others_wrong: Lactic acid and lactate dehydrogenase belong to fermentation, not to this operon, and the name has nothing to do with the lac insect.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option A: Lactose

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For initiation of translation, the ribosome binds to the mRNA at the start codon AUG, which is recognised only by the initiator tRNA.
Statement II: There are no tRNAs for the stop codons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: for initiation, the ribosome binds to the mRNA at the start codon (AUG) that is recognised only by the initiator tRNA (Statement I true). In discussing tRNA, NCERT notes that there are specific tRNAs for every amino acid and an initiator tRNA, but there are no tRNAs for stop codons; at the stop codon a release factor binds and terminates translation (Statement II true).
steps: Stop codons: no tRNA; release factor
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', tRNA - the adapter molecule; translation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): DNA ligase is required during the replication of E. coli DNA.
Reason (R): E. coli, with 4.6 × 10⁶ bp of DNA, completes replication in about 38 minutes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: DNA polymerases polymerise only in the 5'→3' direction, so replication is continuous on one template strand and discontinuous on the other; the discontinuously synthesised fragments are later joined by DNA ligase (A true). R is a true NCERT statement about the speed of replication (an average rate of about 2000 bp per second), but speed has nothing to do with why ligase is needed. R does not explain A.
steps: A: ligase joins the discontinuous fragments
R: true, about the rate of replication
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (nitrogenous base) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Uracil
B. Thymine
C. Guanine
D. Adenine

List-II:
I. Pyrimidine found in RNA in place of thymine
II. Pyrimidine found in DNA; chemically 5-methyl uracil
III. Purine that pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds
IV. Purine that pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the purines are adenine and guanine; the pyrimidines are cytosine, uracil and thymine. Uracil is found in RNA at the place of thymine (A-I); thymine, present in DNA, is 5-methyl uracil (B-II). Guanine pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds (C-III) and adenine with thymine through two (D-IV).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap uracil with thymine, or guanine with adenine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a eukaryotic nucleus, DNA is wrapped around the histone octamer to form the nucleosome.
Reason (R): DNA is negatively charged, whereas the histone octamer is positively charged.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: histones are positively charged, being rich in the basic residues lysine and arginine. The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form the nucleosome. The opposite charges allow the DNA to wrap around the octamer, so R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT uses the sentence RAM HAS RED CAP, read as three-letter words, to explain mutations. Inserting the two letters BI between HAS and RED gives RAM HAS BIR EDC AP. In a gene, this corresponds to:

options.text: Insertion of one codon, adding one amino acid with the reading frame unaltered
A base substitution that changes a single amino acid
Insertion of two bases, shifting the reading frame from the point of insertion
Deletion of two bases, with the reading frame restored at once

solution.explanation: NCERT: inserting one or two bases changes the reading frame from the point of insertion, as RAM HAS BIR EDC AP shows: every word after the insertion is altered. Inserting or deleting three (or a multiple of three) bases adds or removes one or more codons (RAM HAS BIG RED CAP), and the reading frame remains unaltered from that point onwards. Such insertions and deletions are frame-shift insertion or deletion mutations.
solution.why_others_wrong: Adding a whole codon corresponds to inserting three letters (BIG); a substitution would change one word only; nothing was deleted here.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code: mutations and genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option C: Insertion of two bases, shifting the reading frame from the point of insertion

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Wild-type E. coli growing without glucose is given lactose. Which of the following take place, according to NCERT?

(a) Lactose enters the cell through the permease made by the low level of lac operon expression always present.
(b) The repressor is inactivated by interaction with the inducer.
(c) RNA polymerase gains access to the promoter and transcribes the z, y and a genes.
(d) The i gene stops making the repressor.
(e) β-Galactosidase hydrolyses lactose into galactose and glucose.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a very low level of lac operon expression is always present, since without permease lactose cannot enter the cell (a). In the presence of the inducer, the repressor is inactivated by interaction with it (b), allowing RNA polymerase access to the promoter, and transcription of the polycistronic z, y, a genes proceeds (c). β-Galactosidase hydrolyses lactose into galactose and glucose (e). The repressor is synthesised all the time (constitutively) from the i gene; it is inactivated, not stopped (d false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) wrongly stop repressor synthesis; '(a), (c) and (e)' omits the inactivation of the repressor.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the Hershey–Chase experiment, bacteriophages grown on a medium containing radioactive sulphur had radioactive protein but not radioactive DNA.
Reason (R): Proteins contain sulphur, whereas DNA does not contain sulphur.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: viruses grown on radioactive sulphur contained radioactive protein but not radioactive DNA, because DNA does not contain sulphur. In the same way, phosphorus labelled only the DNA, because DNA contains phosphorus but protein does not. R is exactly the reason for A.
steps: Sulphur: in protein, not in DNA
So ³⁵S labels only the protein coat
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material: the genetic material is DNA
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Since 61 codons code for only 20 amino acids, some amino acids are coded by more than one codon.
Statement II: Codons in an mRNA are separated from one another by punctuations.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: of the 64 triplet codons, 61 code for amino acids and 3 are stop codons. With 61 codons for 20 amino acids, some amino acids are coded by more than one codon; hence the code is degenerate (Statement I true). The codon is read in mRNA in a contiguous fashion; there are no punctuations (Statement II false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (stage of translation) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Charging of tRNA
B. Initiation
C. Elongation
D. Termination

List-II:
I. A release factor binds to the stop codon
II. Amino acids are activated in the presence of ATP and linked to their cognate tRNA
III. The ribosome binds to the mRNA at the start codon, recognised only by the initiator tRNA
IV. Amino acid–tRNA complexes sequentially bind to the appropriate codons by base pairing with the anticodons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: amino acids are activated in the presence of ATP and linked to their cognate tRNA, called charging or aminoacylation of tRNA (A-II). For initiation, the ribosome binds to the mRNA at the start codon AUG, recognised only by the initiator tRNA (B-III). During elongation, complexes of an amino acid linked to tRNA sequentially bind to the appropriate codon by forming complementary base pairs with the tRNA anticodon (C-IV). At the end, a release factor binds to the stop codon, terminating translation (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap charging with initiation, initiation with elongation, or charging with termination.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', translation
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Regulation of the lac operon by the repressor is referred to as negative regulation.
Reason (R): The lac repressor acts by binding to the promoter of the operon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the absence of an inducer, the repressor binds to the operator region of the operon and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing it; regulation by the repressor is therefore negative regulation (A true). The repressor binds to the operator, not the promoter; the promoter is the binding site of RNA polymerase (R false).
steps: Promoter: RNA polymerase site → R false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements comparing the classic experiments are correct, according to NCERT?

(a) Griffith showed transformation but could not establish the biochemical nature of the 'transforming principle'.
(b) Avery, MacLeod and McCarty found that digestion with DNase inhibited transformation.
(c) Hershey and Chase provided the unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material.
(d) Meselson and Stahl's experiment proved that DNA, not protein, is the genetic material.
(e) Griffith used bacteriophages infecting E. coli in his experiments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: Griffith's experiments showed that R strain bacteria were transformed by heat-killed S strain, but the biochemical nature of the transforming principle was not defined (a). Avery, MacLeod and McCarty found that proteases and RNases did not affect transformation, but DNase did inhibit it (b). The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from Hershey and Chase (c). Meselson and Stahl showed that DNA replicates semiconservatively (d false), and Griffith worked with Streptococcus pneumoniae and mice (e false).
steps: Avery et al.: DNase blocks it
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) misassign the Meselson–Stahl finding or Griffith's organism; '(b), (c) and (e)' also omits (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material; replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: At a replication fork, one new strand is synthesised continuously and the other discontinuously. Which feature is common to BOTH?

options.text: The new fragments must be joined later by DNA ligase
The new strand is polymerised in the 5'→3' direction by DNA-dependent DNA polymerase
The new strand is polymerised in the 3'→5' direction

solution.explanation: NCERT: DNA-dependent DNA polymerases catalyse polymerisation only in one direction, 5'→3'. Consequently, on the template with 3'→5' polarity replication is continuous, while on the template with 5'→3' polarity it is discontinuous, and these discontinuous fragments are later joined by DNA ligase. Both new strands are made 5'→3'.
solution.why_others_wrong: A 3'→5' template and continuous synthesis go together, so that feature belongs to one strand only; ligase joins only the discontinuous fragments; and no strand is made 3'→5'.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option C: The new strand is polymerised in the 5'→3' direction by DNA-dependent DNA polymerase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: NCERT calls the Human Genome Project a 'mega project'. Which reason does it give?

options.text: The human genome has about 3 × 10⁹ bp, and at an estimated US $3 per bp sequencing would cost about 9 billion US dollars, with an enormous amount of data to store
It was carried out by a single laboratory over a period of 50 years
It sequenced the genomes of all living organisms on earth
It required the sequencing of only the protein-coding 2 per cent of the genome

solution.concept: Why the HGP was a mega project
solution.explanation: NCERT: the human genome is said to have approximately 3 × 10⁹ bp; if the cost of sequencing was US $3 per bp (the estimated cost in the beginning), the total cost would be approximately 9 billion US dollars. Further, if the sequence were stored in typed form in books, 3300 books of 1000 pages each would be needed. These huge numbers made it a mega project.
solution.why_others_wrong: The HGP was an international effort (1990–2003), was not about all organisms (though several model organisms were also sequenced), and sequenced the whole genome, coding and non-coding.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', Human Genome Project
solution.final_answer: Option A: The human genome has about 3 × 10⁹ bp, and at an estimated US $3 per bp sequencing would cost about 9 billion US dollars, with an enormous amount of data to store

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: E. coli grown for many generations in ¹⁵NH₄Cl medium is transferred to ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium for two generations and then returned to ¹⁵NH₄Cl medium for one more generation. Replication is semiconservative. What fractions of the DNA molecules are now heavy (¹⁵N/¹⁵N), hybrid (¹⁵N/¹⁴N) and light (¹⁴N/¹⁴N)?

solution.explanation: Start: one H/H molecule. Generation 1 in ¹⁴N: 2 H/L. Generation 2 in ¹⁴N: each H/L gives one H/L and one L/L → 2 H/L + 2 L/L. Generation 3 in ¹⁵N: every old strand pairs with a new heavy strand; H/L gives H/H + L/H, and L/L gives L/H + L/H. Total 8 molecules: 2 H/H (heavy) and 6 hybrid, none light → 1/4 heavy, 3/4 hybrid.
steps: After 2 generations in ¹⁴N: 2 hybrid, 2 light
In ¹⁵N every new strand is heavy
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/2 heavy, 1/2 hybrid is the result of only one generation in ¹⁴N before the return to ¹⁵N; the '3/4 light' answer ignores the last generation in ¹⁵N; a light class cannot remain because every molecule made in ¹⁵N carries a new heavy strand.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option B: 1/4 heavy, 3/4 hybrid, none light

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A single base substitution within the coding region of a gene always changes the amino acid sequence of the polypeptide.
Reason (R): Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the code is degenerate, since some amino acids are coded by more than one codon (R true); e.g. UUU and UUC both code for phenylalanine. A substitution that turns one such codon into another codon for the same amino acid leaves the polypeptide unchanged, so a base substitution does not always change the sequence (A false). (A substitution can change an amino acid, as GAG → GUG in sickle-cell anaemia, but not always.)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code; mutations and genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A nucleic acid sample has the base composition: adenine 20%, uracil 30%, guanine 25% and cytosine 25%. Which inferences are correct?

(a) The sample is RNA.
(b) It cannot be a double-stranded molecule in which all bases are paired complementarily.
(c) Its sugar is 2'-deoxyribose.
(d) Chargaff's rule A = T applies to it.
(e) Its purines equal its pyrimidines in amount.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Uracil is found in RNA at the place of thymine, so the sample is RNA (a), with ribose rather than 2'-deoxyribose (c false). If every base were paired complementarily, A would equal U and G would equal C; here A (20%) ≠ U (30%), so the molecule is not fully double-stranded (b). There is no thymine, so A = T cannot apply (d false). Purines A + G = 45% while pyrimidines U + C = 55% (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: (c), (d) and (e) are false: the sugar is ribose, the sample has no thymine, and purines (45%) do not equal pyrimidines (55%).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT's comparison of DNA and RNA as genetic material, which statement is correct?

options.text: RNA, being more stable, is preferred for storage, whereas DNA is better for the transmission of genetic information
DNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins, whereas RNA depends on DNA to express characters
DNA and RNA are equally stable and equally suited to both storage and transmission

DNA, being more stable, is preferred for the storage of genetic information, whereas RNA, which can directly code for the synthesis of proteins, is better for the transmission (expression) of genetic information

solution.concept: Storage versus transmission of genetic information
solution.explanation: NCERT: both DNA and RNA can mutate, but RNA, being unstable, mutates at a faster rate. RNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins and hence can easily express the characters; DNA depends on RNA for protein synthesis. DNA, being more stable, is preferred for the storage of genetic information; for the transmission of genetic information, RNA is better.
steps: RNA: codes directly for proteins → transmission/expression
solution.why_others_wrong: The first and second distractors swap the roles of DNA and RNA; NCERT states that DNA is more stable than RNA, so they are not equally stable or equally suited.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material: properties of genetic material (DNA versus RNA)
solution.final_answer: Option D: DNA, being more stable, is preferred for the storage of genetic information, whereas RNA, which can directly code for the synthesis of proteins, is better for the transmission (expression) of genetic information

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: By a chromosomal rearrangement, an actively expressed gene comes to lie in a region of chromatin that is densely packed and stains dark. On the basis of NCERT's account of chromatin, the most likely result is that the gene:

options.text: Becomes transcriptionally inactive, as such chromatin (heterochromatin) is inactive
Becomes more actively transcribed, as dark-staining chromatin is euchromatin
Is lost from the cell, since heterochromatin is not replicated
Is transcribed only by RNA polymerase III, which acts on heterochromatin

solution.explanation: NCERT: in a typical nucleus, some regions of chromatin are loosely packed and stain light (euchromatin), and others are densely packed and stain dark (heterochromatin). Euchromatin is said to be transcriptionally active, and heterochromatin inactive. A gene moved into heterochromatin is therefore expected to be inactive.
solution.why_others_wrong: Euchromatin is the loosely packed, light-staining, active form; NCERT does not say heterochromatin is lost or left unreplicated, and RNA polymerase III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs, not genes in heterochromatin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option A: Becomes transcriptionally inactive, as such chromatin (heterochromatin) is inactive

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (item for a gene whose coding strand reads 5'-ATGCATTGA-3') with List-II (sequence).

List-I:
A. The mRNA
B. The template strand, written 5'→3'
C. Anticodon of the tRNA for the second codon, written 5'→3'
D. The last codon of the mRNA

List-II:
I. 5'-AUGCAUUGA-3'
II. 5'-TCAATGCAT-3'
III. 5'-AUG-3'
IV. UGA

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Coding strand, template strand, mRNA and anticodon
solution.explanation: NCERT: the mRNA has the same sequence as the coding strand, with uracil in place of thymine: 5'-AUGCAUUGA-3' (A-I). The template strand is complementary and antiparallel; written 5'→3' it is 5'-TCAATGCAT-3' (B-II). The second codon is CAU; its anticodon, complementary and antiparallel, is 5'-AUG-3' (C-III). The last codon UGA is a stop codon (D-IV).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes take the template for the mRNA, or confuse the anticodon of codon 2 with the stop codon, or write the template strand as the anticodon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription; genetic code; tRNA
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In eukaryotes, a failure of cell division after DNA replication results in polyploidy.
Reason (R): Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates serve both as substrates and as a source of energy for DNA polymerisation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in eukaryotes, DNA replication takes place in the S-phase, and replication and cell division must be highly coordinated; a failure in cell division after DNA replication results in polyploidy (A true). R is also a true NCERT line, about the dual role of dNTPs, but it concerns the chemistry of polymerisation, not the consequence of failed division. R does not explain A.
steps: A: replicated DNA without division → polyploidy
R: dNTPs as substrate and energy, unrelated
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT lists diseases, with their common Indian names, that antibiotics have greatly improved our capacity to treat. The disease called 'gal ghotu' is:

solution.explanation: NCERT: antibiotics have greatly improved our capacity to treat deadly diseases such as plague, whooping cough (kali khansi), diphtheria (gal ghotu) and leprosy (kusht rog), which used to kill millions all over the globe.
solution.why_others_wrong: Whooping cough is 'kali khansi' and leprosy is 'kusht rog'; NCERT gives no such local name for plague.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in industrial products: antibiotics
solution.final_answer: Option C: Diphtheria

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, biogas plants are more often built in:

options.text: Rural areas, where cattle dung is available in large quantities
Deserts, where there is plenty of sunlight
Coastal areas, where sea water is available

solution.explanation: NCERT: the excreta (dung) of cattle, commonly called gobar, is rich in methanogenic bacteria and is used to generate biogas (gobar gas). Biogas plants are more often built in rural areas, where cattle dung is available in large quantities. The gas is used for cooking and lighting.
steps: Abundant in rural areas → plants built there
solution.why_others_wrong: The plant needs a regular supply of cattle dung, which is available in rural areas; sunlight or sea water plays no part in biogas production.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in production of biogas
solution.final_answer: Option A: Rural areas, where cattle dung is available in large quantities

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Toddy', a traditional drink of some parts of southern India, is made by fermenting sap from palms.
Reason (R): Lactic acid bacteria improve the nutritional quality of curd by increasing its vitamin B₁₂ content.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: toddy is made by fermenting sap from palms (A true). It also says that lactic acid bacteria increase vitamin B₁₂ in curd (R true). R concerns a different product and a different microbe, so it does not explain how toddy is made.
steps: Different products → R does not explain A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A farmer wants to protect a cabbage crop (a brassica) from butterfly caterpillars without harming the other insects in the field. Which measure described in NCERT suits this aim?

options.text: Spraying a suspension of Bacillus thuringiensis spores on the plants

solution.concept: Bt as a selective biocontrol agent
solution.explanation: NCERT: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is available as dried spores, mixed with water and sprayed onto vulnerable plants such as brassicas and fruit trees, where they are eaten by insect larvae. In the gut the toxin is released and the larvae are killed. The bacterial disease kills the caterpillars but leaves other insects unharmed.
solution.why_others_wrong: Dragonflies control mosquitoes; Glomus is a mycorrhizal fungus that helps absorb phosphorus; and broad-spectrum chemicals kill useful insects as well.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option B: Spraying a suspension of Bacillus thuringiensis spores on the plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Compare the aeration tanks with the anaerobic sludge digesters of a sewage treatment plant. Which statements are correct?

(a) Aerobic microbes grow in the aeration tanks, whereas bacteria that grow anaerobically act in the digesters.
(b) The growth of flocs in the aeration tanks reduces the BOD of the effluent.
(c) The digestion in the digesters produces gases such as methane, hydrogen sulphide and carbon dioxide, which form biogas.
(d) Both are part of the primary treatment of sewage.
(e) The digesters receive the effluent, while the aeration tanks receive the activated sludge.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in secondary (biological) treatment, the primary effluent is passed into aeration tanks, where vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs consumes organic matter and reduces the BOD (a, b). The major part of the activated sludge from the settling tank is pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters, where bacteria growing anaerobically digest the bacteria and fungi in the sludge, producing methane, hydrogen sulphide and CO₂ (biogas) (a, c). Both steps belong to secondary treatment (d false), and it is the effluent that goes to the aeration tank and the sludge to the digester (e false).
steps: Aeration tank: effluent, aerobic flocs, BOD down
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) put the steps in primary treatment or reverse what each unit receives; '(b), (c) and (e)' also omits (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A village wants to set up a biogas plant on cattle dung and to farm organically. Which of the following NCERT statements support this plan?

(a) The spent slurry removed from a biogas plant can be used as fertiliser.
(b) Cattle dung is rich in methanogenic bacteria.
(c) The biogas produced can be used for cooking and lighting.
(d) Bt spores can control caterpillars on brassicas without harming other insects.
(e) Biogas consists predominantly of carbon dioxide and so cannot be burnt.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Biogas and biocontrol in a village
solution.explanation: NCERT: cattle dung (gobar) is rich in methanogenic bacteria (b) and is fed as a slurry into the biogas plant; the spent slurry is removed through another outlet and may be used as fertiliser (a); the biogas is supplied to nearby houses for cooking and lighting (c). Bt spores kill caterpillars but leave other insects unharmed, suiting an organic farm (d). Biogas is predominantly methane and is inflammable (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) are wrong because biogas is mainly methane and burns; '(a), (c) and (d)' leaves out (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in production of biogas; microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Rhizobium and Anabaena both fix atmospheric nitrogen, but only Rhizobium does so in symbiotic association with the root nodules of leguminous plants.
Statement II: Glomus and Trichoderma are both fungi, but only Glomus is described by NCERT as forming mycorrhiza that helps the plant absorb phosphorus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in the root nodules of leguminous plants, while cyanobacteria such as Anabaena, Nostoc and Oscillatoria fix nitrogen as autotrophic microbes in aquatic and terrestrial environments, e.g. in paddy fields (Statement I true). Many members of the genus Glomus form mycorrhiza and absorb phosphorus from the soil for the plant; Trichoderma species are free-living fungi in root ecosystems, used as biocontrol agents against plant pathogens (Statement II true).
steps: Rhizobium: nodules; Anabaena: free, paddy fields
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers; microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, it is not surprising that parasitism has evolved in so many taxonomic groups, from plants to higher vertebrates, because the parasitic mode of life:

options.text: Always benefits both the parasite and the host
Requires no adaptation by the parasite
Allows the parasite to avoid having any host

solution.explanation: NCERT: considering that the parasitic mode of life ensures free lodging and meals, it is not surprising that parasitism has evolved in so many taxonomic groups from plants to higher vertebrates. Parasites have in turn evolved special adaptations, such as loss of unnecessary sense organs, adhesive organs or suckers, loss of the digestive system and high reproductive capacity.
steps: Parasite gets shelter (lodging) and food (meals) from the host
solution.why_others_wrong: In parasitism the host is harmed, not benefited; parasites show many special adaptations; and a parasite by definition depends on a host.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism
solution.final_answer: Option B: Ensures free lodging and meals

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT gives two most familiar examples of ectoparasites. They are:

options.text: Liver fluke in humans and the malarial parasite
Cuscuta on hedge plants and the koel in a crow's nest
Copepods on marine fish and tapeworms in humans
Lice on humans and ticks on dogs

solution.explanation: NCERT: parasites that feed on the external surface of the host organism are called ectoparasites; the most familiar examples are the lice on humans and ticks on dogs. Many marine fish are also infested with ectoparasitic copepods. Endoparasites, such as the liver fluke and the malarial parasite, live inside the host body.
steps: Ectoparasite: feeds on the external surface
Examples: lice on humans, ticks on dogs
solution.why_others_wrong: The liver fluke and malarial parasite are endoparasites; the koel is a brood parasite; the tapeworm lives inside the host, so the pair with copepods is mixed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism
solution.final_answer: Option D: Lice on humans and ticks on dogs

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Birth rates and death rates of a population are expressed as per capita births and deaths respectively.
Statement II: An age pyramid with a broad base of pre-reproductive individuals shows a declining population.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: a population has birth rates and death rates, which refer to per capita births and deaths respectively, expressed as change in numbers with respect to members of the population (Statement I true). The shape of the age pyramid reflects the growth status: a broad base (many pre-reproductive individuals) shows an expanding population, a bell shape a stable one and an urn shape (narrow base) a declining one (Statement II false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population attributes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are attributes that a population has but an individual organism does not?

(a) Birth rate
(b) Death rate
(c) Sex ratio
(d) Age distribution
(e) Body size

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a population has certain attributes that an individual organism does not. An individual may have births and deaths, but a population has birth rates and death rates; a population also has a sex ratio and an age distribution. Body size belongs to each individual organism.
steps: Population: birth rate, death rate, sex ratio, age distribution
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) include body size, an attribute of individuals; '(a), (c) and (d)' leaves out the death rate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population attributes
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A population grows according to the logistic model, dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K], in a habitat with carrying capacity K = 800. At what population size will its per capita growth rate, (1/N)(dN/dt), be one-fourth of r?

solution.concept: Per capita growth rate in logistic growth
solution.explanation: Per capita growth rate = (1/N)(dN/dt) = r(K − N)/K. Setting this equal to r/4: (K − N)/K = 1/4, so K − N = 200 and N = 800 − 200 = 600.
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 solves N/K = 1/4 instead of (K − N)/K = 1/4; 400 (= K/2) is where dN/dt, not the per capita rate, is highest; at 800 (= K) the per capita rate is zero.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: growth models (logistic growth)
solution.final_answer: Option C: 600

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In which of the following does NCERT describe co-evolution (or the need for it) between the interacting species?

(a) Many parasites and their hosts, since parasites tend to be host-specific
(b) The fig and its partner wasp species
(c) The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys and the bee that pollinates it
(d) The introduced goats and the Abingdon tortoise of the Galapagos Islands
(e) Cattle egrets and grazing cattle

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: many parasites have evolved to be host-specific (they can parasitise only a single species of host) in such a way that both host and parasite tend to co-evolve (a). Plant-animal interactions often involve co-evolution of the mutualists, as with the fig and its pollinating wasp (b). In Ophrys, if the female bee's colour patterns change even slightly during evolution, pollination success will be reduced unless the orchid flower co-evolves (c). The goats and the tortoise illustrate competition, and cattle egrets and cattle illustrate commensalism; NCERT does not describe co-evolution for them.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) include interactions for which NCERT speaks of competition or commensalism, not co-evolution.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism; mutualism
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lichens represent an intimate mutualistic relationship between a fungus and photosynthesising algae or cyanobacteria.
Reason (R): Mycorrhizae are associations between fungi and the roots of higher plants.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: lichens represent an intimate mutualistic relationship between a fungus and photosynthesising algae or cyanobacteria (A true). Mycorrhizae are associations between fungi and the roots of higher plants (R true). R describes a different association, involving plant roots, and says nothing about the partners in a lichen, so it does not explain A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: mutualism
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Both the exponential and the logistic models of population growth contain the intrinsic rate of natural increase, r.
Statement II: The integral form Nₜ = N₀e^(rt) describes logistic growth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: exponential growth is dN/dt = rN, whose integral form is Nₜ = N₀e^(rt); logistic growth is dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K]. Both contain r (Statement I true). The integral form Nₜ = N₀e^(rt) is that of exponential growth; it has no carrying capacity K, so it cannot describe logistic growth (Statement II false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: growth models
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (phase of logistic (sigmoid) growth) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Lag phase
B. Phase of acceleration
C. Phase of deceleration
D. Asymptote

List-II:
I. The population density reaches the carrying capacity
II. Initial phase of slow growth
III. Growth slows as the limited resources begin to restrict the population
IV. Population numbers increase rapidly

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows initially a lag phase (A-II), followed by phases of acceleration (B-IV) and deceleration (C-III), and finally an asymptote, when the population density reaches the carrying capacity (D-I). Plotting N against time gives a sigmoid curve.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the lag and acceleration phases, the deceleration phase and the asymptote, or acceleration and deceleration.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: growth models (logistic growth)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Two populations, P and Q, each start with 1000 individuals and grow exponentially (Nₜ = N₀e^(rt)), P with r = 0.03 per year and Q with r = 0.015 per year. Taking ln 2 = 0.693, what will be their sizes after 46.2 years?

solution.explanation: rt for P = 0.03 × 46.2 = 1.386 = 2 × 0.693 = 2 ln 2, so e^(rt) = 2² = 4 and P = 4000. For Q, rt = 0.015 × 46.2 = 0.693 = ln 2, so e^(rt) = 2 and Q = 2000. Halving r halves the number of doublings in the same time.
solution.why_others_wrong: '2000 and 1000' leaves Q unchanged and doubles P only once; '2386 and 1693' adds 1000 × rt as if growth were linear; '4000 and 1000' ignores Q's growth.
