questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Large amounts of water can be reabsorbed from the collecting duct to produce a concentrated urine.
Statement II: The collecting duct allows passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium to keep up the osmolarity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the long collecting duct extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts of the medulla. Large amounts of water could be reabsorbed from this region to produce a concentrated urine. This segment allows passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium to keep up the osmolarity, and it also helps maintain the pH and ionic balance of blood by the selective secretion of H⁺ and K⁺.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (substance) with List-II (description in NCERT).

A. Ammonia

III. Formed from ammonia in the liver of ureotelic animals

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Forms of nitrogenous and other wastes
solution.explanation: NCERT: ammonia is the most toxic form and requires large amounts of water for its elimination; in ureotelic animals ammonia is converted into urea in the liver; uric acid, being the least toxic, can be removed with a minimum loss of water as pellet or paste; the liver secretes bile containing bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins and drugs, which pass out with digestive wastes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly compares the PCT and the DCT of a human nephron?

options.text: Both lie in the cortex; the PCT reabsorbs nearly all the essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of the electrolytes and water, whereas the DCT carries out conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water
Both lie in the medulla; the PCT carries out conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, whereas the DCT reabsorbs nearly all the essential nutrients
Both lie in the cortex; the PCT carries out conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, whereas the DCT reabsorbs nearly all the essential nutrients
The PCT lies in the cortex and the DCT in the medulla; only the PCT secretes H⁺ and K⁺

solution.explanation: NCERT: the Malpighian corpuscle, PCT and DCT are situated in the cortical region of the kidney. Nearly all the essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of electrolytes and water are reabsorbed by the PCT. Conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water takes place in the DCT. Both secrete H⁺ and K⁺ (the PCT also ammonia, the DCT also NH₃) to maintain pH and ionic balance.
steps: DCT → conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water
solution.why_others_wrong: B puts both in the medulla and swaps their roles; C swaps their roles; D puts the DCT in the medulla and denies its secretion of H⁺ and K⁺.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', human excretory system – nephron; urine formation – function of the tubules
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both lie in the cortex; the PCT reabsorbs nearly all the essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of the electrolytes and water, whereas the DCT carries out conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
NCERT describes certain parts of the nephron as helping to maintain the pH and ionic balance of the body fluids or blood by the selective secretion of H⁺ and K⁺. Which of the following are such parts?

(a) Proximal convoluted tubule
(b) Distal convoluted tubule
(c) Collecting duct
(d) Descending limb of Henle's loop
(e) Bowman's capsule

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the PCT helps maintain the pH and ionic balance of the body fluids by selective secretion of H⁺, ammonia and K⁺ into the filtrate and absorption of HCO₃⁻; the DCT is capable of reabsorbing HCO₃⁻ and selectively secreting H⁺, K⁺ and NH₃ to maintain pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood; the collecting duct plays a role in maintaining pH and ionic balance of blood by selective secretion of H⁺ and K⁺. The descending limb is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes, and Bowman's capsule receives the filtrate.
solution.why_others_wrong: A leaves out the collecting duct; B adds Bowman's capsule; C adds the descending limb and leaves out the PCT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation – function of the tubules
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:

Assertion (A): Henle's loop plays a significant role in the maintenance of a high osmolarity of the medullary interstitial fluid.
Reason (R): Reabsorption in Henle's loop is the maximum of all the segments of the renal tubule.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: reabsorption in Henle's loop is MINIMUM, but this segment plays a significant role in the maintenance of high osmolarity of the medullary interstitial fluid. The maximum reabsorption occurs in the PCT (nearly all essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of electrolytes and water).

solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept the false Reason; D rejects the true Assertion.

solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Both ADH and angiotensin II, through their constrictory effects on blood vessels, can increase the glomerular filtration rate.
Statement II: Both ADH and aldosterone are released into the blood from the neurohypophysis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Comparing the hormones that regulate the kidney
solution.explanation: NCERT: ADH can affect kidney function by its constrictory effects on blood vessels, which increases blood pressure and can increase the glomerular blood flow and thereby the GFR. Angiotensin II, a powerful vasoconstrictor, increases the glomerular blood pressure and thereby the GFR. ADH is released from the neurohypophysis, but aldosterone is released by the adrenal cortex (activated by angiotensin II).

Statement II → false: aldosterone comes from the adrenal cortex

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (condition) with List-II (expected consequence according to NCERT).

List-I:
A. Deficiency of ADH
B. Diabetes mellitus
C. Destruction of the JG cells
D. Excess of atrial natriuretic factor

List-II:
I. Vasodilation and a fall in blood pressure
II. No renin is released when the glomerular blood flow falls
III. Glucose and ketone bodies appear in the urine
IV. Water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule falls, so diuresis is not prevented

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: ADH facilitates water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule, thereby preventing diuresis – its deficiency removes this; glycosuria and ketonuria are indicative of diabetes mellitus; a fall in glomerular blood flow activates the JG cells to release renin – without JG cells this cannot happen; ANF causes vasodilation and thereby decreases blood pressure.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps diabetes mellitus and the JG cells; C swaps ADH deficiency and diabetes mellitus; D swaps the JG cells and ANF.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Suppose the collecting duct of a person's nephrons no longer allowed urea to pass into the medullary interstitium, while every other part of the kidney worked normally. Using NCERT's account, which effect is expected?

options.text: It would be harder to keep up the osmolarity of the medullary interstitium, so the ability to form concentrated urine would fall
Glucose would begin to appear in the urine
The glomerular filtration rate would rise sharply
The ascending limb of Henle's loop would become permeable to water

solution.concept: Urea and the medullary osmolarity gradient
solution.explanation: NCERT: the collecting duct allows passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium to keep up the osmolarity. Together with the counter-current mechanism, this maintains the concentration gradient in the medullary interstitium, and the gradient helps the easy passage of water from the collecting tubule, concentrating the filtrate. Without the urea contribution, the gradient – and hence urine concentration – would suffer.
steps: Urea into interstitium → keeps up medullary osmolarity
Gradient → water leaves the collecting duct → concentrated urine
No urea entry → weaker concentrating ability
solution.why_others_wrong: B depends on glucose reabsorption in the PCT; C depends on glomerular blood pressure; D is unrelated – the ascending limb stays impermeable to water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation – function of the tubules; mechanism of concentration of the filtrate
solution.final_answer: Option A: It would be harder to keep up the osmolarity of the medullary interstitium, so the ability to form concentrated urine would fall

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly arranges the organisation of a skeletal muscle from the largest unit to the smallest?

Fascicles → muscle → muscle fibres → myofibrils → actin and myosin filaments

Which of the following statements correctly describe the axon of a neuron, as given in NCERT?

The functioning of vital involuntary organs such as the lungs, heart and kidneys
Only the processing of vision and hearing; memory and emotions are handled by the PNS
Only the activities of endocrine glands, not human behaviour

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Within a fraction of a second after a site on an axon is stimulated, the resting potential is restored at that site.
Reason (R): The rise in Na⁺ permeability at the site is extremely short-lived and is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺, so that K⁺ diffuses to the outside of the membrane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the rise in the stimulus-induced permeability to Na⁺ is extremely short-lived. It is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺. Within a fraction of a second, K⁺ diffuses outside the membrane and restores the resting potential of the membrane at the site of excitation, and the fibre becomes once more responsive to further stimulation. The events in R are what restore the resting potential, so R explains A.
steps: Short-lived Na⁺ rise + K⁺ outflow -> resting potential restored
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; NCERT presents the outward diffusion of K⁺ after the brief Na⁺ rise as the process that restores the resting potential, so R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Generation and Conduction of Nerve Impulse
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: At a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane. What, according to NCERT, is the immediate result of this binding?

Electrical current flows directly from the pre-synaptic into the post-synaptic neuron
The post-synaptic membrane becomes permanently impermeable to all ions
Ion channels open, allowing entry of ions that can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron

solution.explanation: NCERT: the released neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors present on the post-synaptic membrane. This binding opens ion channels, allowing the entry of ions which can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron. The new potential developed may be either excitatory or inhibitory.
steps: Binding to receptors -> ion channels open
Ions enter -> new potential (excitatory or inhibitory)
solution.why_others_wrong: Synaptic vesicles are in the pre-synaptic knob, not the post-synaptic neuron; direct current flow happens at electrical synapses, which have no neurotransmitters; and the binding opens channels rather than closing the membrane to all ions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Transmission of Impulses
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ion channels open, allowing entry of ions that can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
An axon is at rest. Which of the following are TRUE of it, according to NCERT?

(a) The axonal membrane is nearly impermeable to Na⁺.
(b) The axonal membrane is impermeable to the negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm.
(c) The outer surface of the axonal membrane is negatively charged.
(d) The concentration of K⁺ is higher in the axoplasm than in the fluid outside.
(e) The membrane is in a depolarised state.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: when a neuron is not conducting any impulse, i.e. resting, the axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to K⁺ and nearly impermeable to Na⁺; it is also impermeable to the negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm. The axoplasm contains a high concentration of K⁺ and negatively charged proteins and a low concentration of Na⁺. The outer surface carries a positive charge and the inner surface a negative charge, so the membrane is POLARISED; a depolarised membrane is found only at a stimulated site.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) reverses the resting charges and (e) describes a stimulated site, so options with either are wrong; the remaining statements (a), (b) and (d) are all NCERT facts about the resting state.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Generation and Conduction of Nerve Impulse
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology

Match List-I (feature) with List-II (neural structure).

A. Has one axon and one dendrite
B. Gap between two adjacent myelin sheaths
C. Enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon
D. Granular bodies present in the cell body and dendrites

List-II:
I. Unmyelinated nerve fibre
II. Nissl's granules
III. Bipolar neuron
IV. Node of Ranvier

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: bipolar neurons have one axon and one dendrite (found in the retina). In myelinated fibres, the gaps between two adjacent myelin sheaths are called nodes of Ranvier. An unmyelinated nerve fibre is enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon. Nissl's granules are certain granular bodies in the cytoplasm of the cell body, also present in the dendrites.
solution.why_others_wrong: A node of Ranvier is a gap between myelin sheaths, not a fibre wrapped by a non-myelinating Schwann cell; Nissl's granules are granular bodies, not a type of neuron; and a bipolar neuron is a neuron, not an unmyelinated fibre.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Neuron as Structural and Functional Unit of Neural System
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An electrical synapse can transmit an impulse even though no neurotransmitter is released across it.
Reason (R): At an electrical synapse, the pre- and post-synaptic membranes are separated by a fluid-filled synaptic cleft.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: at electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, and electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across these synapses. Neurotransmitters are involved only at chemical synapses, where the membranes are separated by a fluid-filled space called the synaptic cleft. A is true; R wrongly gives the electrical synapse the cleft of a chemical synapse.
steps: R: false - the synaptic cleft belongs to a chemical synapse
solution.why_others_wrong: R is false, so options treating both statements as true are wrong; A is true because current passes directly between the closely apposed membranes, so 'A is false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 18 'Neural Control and Coordination', Transmission of Impulses
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following structures of the human brain belong to the MIDBRAIN or the HINDBRAIN (i.e. not to the forebrain)?

Cerebrum, thalamus, corpora quadrigemina, pons, hypothalamus, cerebral aqueduct, cerebellum, hippocampus

solution.explanation: NCERT: the forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus; the hippocampus is one of the deep structures that, with the inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres, form the limbic system of the forebrain. The midbrain has the cerebral aqueduct passing through it and the corpora quadrigemina on its dorsal side. The hindbrain comprises the pons, cerebellum and medulla oblongata.

solution.final_answer: Option B: Four

questions.subject: Zoology

solution.explanation: NCERT: the pars distalis produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH, and the pars intermedia secretes only one hormone, MSH. The pars nervosa (neurohypophysis) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus.

Neurohypophysis: releases oxytocin and vasopressin (made in hypothalamus)

questions.subject: Zoology

Mineralocorticoids: water and electrolyte balance -> main one aldosterone

solution.explanation: NCERT: iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid. questions.subject: Zoology

Which of the following hormones are produced by cells of the gonads (testis or ovary)?

(e) Gonadotrophin releasing hormone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: Leydig cells in the intertubular spaces of the testis produce androgens, mainly testosterone. In the ovary, estrogen is synthesised and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles, and the corpus luteum (formed from the ruptured follicle after ovulation) secretes mainly progesterone. FSH is a pars distalis hormone that acts on the gonads, and GnRH is a hypothalamic hormone acting on the pituitary.

questions.question_text: Which of the following actions does NCERT ascribe to BOTH the glucocorticoids (such as cortisol) and the catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline)?

solution.concept: Comparing adrenal cortex and adrenal medulla hormones

Catecholamines increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection and sweating, increase heart beat and rate of respiration, stimulate glycogen breakdown, and also stimulate the breakdown of lipids and proteins. Common: lipids and proteins broken down

steps: R is structure of the gland, A is an action of its hormones -> unrelated

The thyroid gland also secretes a PROTEIN hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT), which regulates the blood calcium level.
steps: Statement I: true (T4 and T3 are iodothyronines)
Statement II: false - TCT is a protein hormone

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A hormone has these three features: it is synthesised by hypothalamic neurons; it is stored in and released from the neurohypophysis; and it acts mainly at the kidney, reducing the loss of water through urine. The hormone is:

solution.concept: Identifying a hormone from its features
solution.explanation: NCERT: the pars nervosa stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are synthesised by the hypothalamus and transported axonally to the neurohypophysis. Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, thereby reducing loss of water through urine (diuresis); hence it is also called the anti-diuretic hormone (ADH).
steps: Hypothalamic synthesis + neurohypophysis release -> oxytocin or vasopressin
Acts on kidney, reduces water loss -> vasopressin (ADH)
solution.why_others_wrong: Oxytocin shares the origin and release route but acts on smooth muscles (uterus, mammary glands), not the kidney; aldosterone and PTH act on renal tubules but come from the adrenal cortex and the parathyroid glands, not from hypothalamic neurons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Hypothalamus; Pituitary Gland

So both involve the thyroid (A true), but cretinism results from HYPOthyroidism (R false).
steps: A: true - both are thyroid disorders
R: false - cretinism is due to hypothyroidism

questions.subject: Zoology

Which of the following statements about the human menstrual cycle are correct, according to NCERT?

(a) The first menstruation, which begins at puberty, is called menarche.

(e) Menstrual cycles cease around 50 years of age; this is termed menopause.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the first menstruation begins at puberty and is called menarche. The cycle is repeated at an average interval of about 28/29 days. The menstrual flow lasts for 3–5 days. Both LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of the cycle (about the 14th day). In human beings, menstrual cycles cease around 50 years of age, termed menopause. 14 days is the time to ovulation, not the length of the cycle.
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) gives the time to the mid-cycle peak instead of the length of the cycle, so options containing (c) are wrong; the correct option keeps all the other four NCERT timings.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a woman, an ovum is fertilised in the ampullary region and the zygote undergoes cleavage to form a morula, but the morula fails to transform into a blastocyst. According to NCERT's sequence of events, which of the following could then NOT take place?

options.text: Attachment of the trophoblast to the endometrium (implantation)
Fusion of the haploid nuclei of the sperm and the ovum
Formation of 2, 4 and 8 blastomeres by mitotic division
Completion of the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte

solution.explanation: NCERT: the morula continues to divide and transforms into a blastocyst as it moves further into the uterus. The blastomeres in the blastocyst are arranged into an outer trophoblast and an inner cell mass. The trophoblast layer then gets attached to the endometrium; the uterine cells divide rapidly and cover the blastocyst, which becomes embedded in the endometrium (implantation). Without a blastocyst there is no trophoblast to attach, so implantation cannot occur. The other events listed come before the morula stage.
steps: Trophoblast attaches to endometrium -> implantation (cannot occur)
solution.why_others_wrong: Fusion of the gametes' nuclei and completion of the second meiotic division happen at fertilisation, and cleavage into 2, 4 and 8 blastomeres produces the morula; all three are already over when the morula fails to form a blastocyst.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and Implantation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Attachment of the trophoblast to the endometrium (implantation)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Oogonia continue to be formed and added to the ovaries throughout the reproductive life of a woman.
Reason (R): Gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed within each fetal ovary during embryonic development.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed within each fetal ovary; no more oogonia are formed and added after birth. So R is true and A is false.
steps: A: false - no oogonia are added after birth
R: true - formed in the fetal ovary
solution.why_others_wrong: A contradicts NCERT's statement that no more oogonia are formed and added after birth, so options calling A true are wrong; R is NCERT's own statement, so 'A is false but R is true' is the answer.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Each human testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules.
Statement II: Each testicular lobule contains about 10 to 12 highly coiled seminiferous tubules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: each testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules, and each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced. 10–12 cm is the length of an oviduct, not the number of tubules.
steps: Statement II: false - one to three tubules per lobule
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II overstates the number of tubules per lobule, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is NCERT's figure, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Male Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which option gives the three layers of the wall of the human uterus in the correct order from the OUTSIDE to the INSIDE (towards the uterine cavity)?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the wall of the uterus has three layers of tissue: the external thin membranous perimetrium, the middle thick layer of smooth muscle, the myometrium, and the inner glandular layer called the endometrium that lines the uterine cavity.
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option lists the layers from inside to outside; the myometrium is the middle layer, not the outermost; and the glandular endometrium lines the cavity, so it cannot lie between the other two.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Female Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option B: Perimetrium → myometrium → endometrium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, each seminiferous tubule of the human testis is lined on its inside by which two types of cells?

options.text: Male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells
Leydig cells and immunologically competent cells

solution.explanation: NCERT: each seminiferous tubule is lined on its inside by two types of cells called male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells. The regions outside the seminiferous tubules, the interstitial spaces, contain small blood vessels and interstitial cells or Leydig cells; other immunologically competent cells are also present there.
steps: Inside the tubule: spermatogonia + Sertoli cells
Outside (interstitial spaces): Leydig cells, blood vessels
solution.why_others_wrong: Leydig cells and immunologically competent cells lie in the interstitial spaces outside the tubules, so every option naming Leydig cells is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Male Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A woman has regular 28-day menstrual cycles. The menstrual flow of one cycle begins on 3 June, which is day 1 of that cycle. Using NCERT's account that ovulation takes place in the middle of the cycle (about the 14th day), on about which date is ovulation expected in this cycle?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the menstrual phase starts the cycle, and both LH and FSH peak in the middle of the cycle (about the 14th day); the LH surge induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum (ovulation). Day 1 is 3 June, so day 14 is 13 days later: 16 June.
solution.shortcut: Day n of the cycle = start date + (n - 1) days.
solution.why_others_wrong: 17 June adds 14 days to day 1 (that is day 15); 1 July is day 29, the start of the next cycle; 10 June (day 8) falls in the follicular phase, before the mid-cycle LH surge.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option D: 16 June

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A human primary oocyte (46 chromosomes) completes its first meiotic division before ovulation, and the secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division when a sperm enters it. Assume the first polar body does not divide further. What is the total number of chromosomes present in the ootid (ovum), the second polar body and the first polar body taken together?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the first meiotic division of the primary oocyte is unequal and gives a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body. When a sperm enters, the secondary oocyte completes the second meiotic division, giving a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid). All three cells are haploid, with 23 chromosomes each.
solution.why_others_wrong: 46 forgets the first polar body; 92 treats the ootid as diploid (46) and adds two haploid polar bodies; 23 counts only the ootid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis; Fertilisation and Implantation
solution.final_answer: Option B: 69

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements correctly compare the human testis and ovary?

(a) Both are primary sex organs that produce gametes as well as hormones.
(b) The testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum, whereas the ovaries lie in the lower abdomen.
(c) Both contain highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which the gametes are produced.
(d) Each testis is about 4 to 5 cm long, whereas each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm long.
(e) The ovarian stroma is divided into a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla, whereas each testicular lobule contains one to three seminiferous tubules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the testes are situated outside the abdominal cavity within a pouch called the scrotum; each testis is oval, about 4 to 5 cm long and 2 to 3 cm wide, with about 250 lobules each containing one to three seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced. The ovaries are located one on each side of the lower abdomen; each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm long, and its stroma is divided into a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla. Both are primary sex organs that produce gametes and hormones. Seminiferous tubules occur only in the testis; ova develop in ovarian follicles.
steps: (c) false - seminiferous tubules only in the testis
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) is false because ova develop in ovarian follicles, so every option with (c) is wrong; '(b), (d) and (e) only' leaves out (a), which is true for both gonads.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Male Reproductive System; The Female Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (event) with List-II (hormone mainly responsible, as described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum
B. Maintenance of the endometrium during the luteal phase
C. Stronger uterine contractions during parturition
D. Secretion of factors by Sertoli cells that help in spermiogenesis

List-II:
I. FSH
II. Oxytocin
III. LH
IV. Progesterone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the rapid secretion of LH (LH surge) in the middle of the cycle induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum. Progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum is essential for maintenance of the endometrium. Oxytocin from the maternal pituitary acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions at parturition. FSH acts on the Sertoli cells and stimulates secretion of some factors which help in the process of spermiogenesis (LH acts on the Leydig cells).
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping LH and FSH puts ovulation under FSH and the Sertoli cells under LH, which acts on the Leydig cells; progesterone maintains the endometrium and oxytocin causes the contractions, so swapping them is wrong; FSH does not cause uterine contractions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual Cycle; Gametogenesis; Parturition and Lactation
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The secondary oocyte released at ovulation is haploid, although it has not yet completed meiosis.
Reason (R): Before ovulation, the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division, which results in a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle grows in size and completes its first meiotic division. It is an unequal division resulting in the formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body. The second meiotic division is completed only when a sperm enters. The haploid state of the ovulated cell is therefore the result of the completed first meiotic division described in R.
steps: A: true - secondary oocyte is haploid, meiosis II pending
R: true - meiosis I completed before ovulation
First meiotic division halves the chromosome number -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; the haploid state comes from the first meiotic division that R describes, so R is the explanation, not an unrelated fact.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During pregnancy, all events of the menstrual cycle stop and there is no menstruation.
Statement II: Menstruation occurs only if the released ovum is not fertilised.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is not fertilised; lack of menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy, though it may also be caused by other underlying causes such as stress or poor health. During pregnancy all events of the menstrual cycle stop and there is no menstruation.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT's own, so options calling either false are wrong. (The converse of II, that every missed period means pregnancy, is NOT claimed: NCERT adds stress and poor health as other causes.)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are produced by the human OVARY (at some stage of the reproductive life of a woman)?

Relaxin, estrogen, hCG, progesterone, hPL, oxytocin, prolactin, secondary oocyte

solution.explanation: NCERT: the ovaries produce the female gamete (ovum, released as the secondary oocyte at ovulation) and several steroid hormones, estrogen and progesterone. In the later phase of pregnancy, relaxin is secreted by the ovary. hCG and hPL are made by the placenta; oxytocin is released from the maternal pituitary and prolactin from the anterior pituitary.
steps: Ovary: secondary oocyte, estrogen, progesterone, relaxin = 4
solution.why_others_wrong: Three usually forgets relaxin, which NCERT says the ovary secretes late in pregnancy; five or six add placental hormones (hCG, hPL) or pituitary hormones (prolactin, oxytocin).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Female Reproductive System; Pregnancy and Embryonic Development
solution.final_answer: Option B: Four

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which pair consists of cells that are BOTH haploid and BOTH formed directly by the second meiotic division?

options.text: Secondary spermatocyte and first polar body

solution.explanation: NCERT: secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids. The secondary oocyte completes the second meiotic division when a sperm enters, forming a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid). Secondary spermatocytes and the first polar body come from the FIRST meiotic division; spermatozoa come from spermatids by spermiogenesis, which involves no division; and the primary oocyte is diploid.
steps: Meiosis I products: secondary spermatocytes, secondary oocyte + first polar body
Meiosis II products: spermatids, ootid + second polar body
solution.why_others_wrong: Secondary spermatocytes and the first polar body are haploid but come from the first meiotic division; a spermatozoon is formed by spermiogenesis, not by a division; the primary oocyte is diploid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: Spermatid and second polar body

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Besides motivating smaller families, NCERT mentions a statutory measure taken to tackle population growth in India: raising the marriageable age. To what ages was it raised?

options.text: 21 years for females and 18 years for males
18 years for both females and males
16 years for females and 18 years for males
18 years for females and 21 years for males

solution.explanation: NCERT: statutory raising of the marriageable age of the female to 18 years and that of the male to 21 years, and incentives given to couples with small families, are two of the other measures taken to tackle the problem of population growth.
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option reverses the two ages; NCERT gives different ages for males and females, so 18 for both is wrong; 16 and 18 are lower than the ages NCERT states.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option D: 18 years for females and 21 years for males

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: If sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are not detected and treated in time, NCERT says they may lead to complications later. Which set lists those complications?

options.text: Pelvic inflammatory diseases, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility and even cancer of the reproductive tract
Diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus and Addison's disease
Colour blindness, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia

solution.explanation: NCERT: early symptoms of most STIs are minor, and infected females may often be asymptomatic, so infections may remain undetected or untreated for a long time. This could lead to complications later, which include pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract.
steps: Untreated STIs -> PID, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility, cancer of the reproductive tract
solution.why_others_wrong: The other sets are hormonal disorders (thyroid, ADH, insulin, adrenal cortex) or inherited genetic disorders, none of which NCERT links to untreated STIs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Pelvic inflammatory diseases, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility and even cancer of the reproductive tract

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: 'Nirodh' is a popular brand of condom for the male.
Statement II: Unlike diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults, male and female condoms are reusable.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex sheath; 'Nirodh' is a popular brand of condom for the male. Both the male and the female condoms are DISPOSABLE, can be self-inserted and thereby give privacy to the user. It is the diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults (also made of rubber) that are reusable.
steps: Statement II: false - condoms are disposable; diaphragms, caps and vaults are reusable
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses NCERT's contrast between disposable condoms and reusable diaphragms, caps and vaults, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is NCERT's own, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lactational amenorrhea is a natural method of contraception.
Reason (R): The chances of failure of natural methods of contraception are high.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of the ovum and sperms meeting; periodic abstinence, withdrawal (coitus interruptus) and lactational amenorrhea are such methods. Since no medicines or devices are used, side effects are almost nil, but the chances of failure are also high. A method is natural because it uses no device, medicine or surgery, not because it often fails; so R, though true, does not explain A.
steps: R is a limitation of natural methods, not the reason a method is called natural
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; a high failure rate is a drawback of natural methods, not what makes lactational amenorrhea one, so R is not the explanation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (contraceptive) with List-II (type).

List-I:
A. Vaults
B. Multiload 375
C. Implants under the skin
D. Periodic abstinence

List-II:
I. Natural method
II. Barrier method
III. Progestogens alone or with estrogen given by the female
IV. Copper-releasing IUD

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are barriers made of rubber, inserted into the female tract to cover the cervix during coitus. Copper-releasing IUDs are CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375. Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen can be used by females as injections or implants under the skin. Periodic abstinence is a natural method.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A large number of couples all over the world, including India, are infertile. Which of the following does NCERT list as possible reasons for infertility?

(a) Physical reasons
(b) Congenital diseases
(c) Drugs
(d) Immunological reasons
(e) Psychological reasons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: infertility is the inability to conceive or produce children even after unprotected sexual co-habitation. The reasons for this could be many: physical, congenital diseases, drugs, immunological or even psychological. All five listed causes are therefore in NCERT's list.
steps: (a)-(e) all appear in NCERT's list: physical, congenital diseases, drugs, immunological, psychological
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT includes immunological and even psychological reasons alongside physical causes, congenital diseases and drugs, so every option that leaves out any of them is incomplete.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Advertisements and posters in India often show a happy couple with two children and the slogan 'Hum Do Hamare Do' (we two, our two). According to NCERT, what is the purpose of such campaigns?

options.text: To encourage medical termination of every third pregnancy
To promote amniocentesis for choosing the sex of the two children
To motivate smaller families by using contraceptive methods, so as to check population growth
To encourage assisted reproductive technologies for every couple

solution.explanation: NCERT: the most important step to overcome the population explosion is to motivate smaller families by using various contraceptive methods. Advertisements showing a happy couple with two children and the slogan Hum Do Hamare Do serve this aim; many couples, mostly the young, urban, working ones, have even adopted a 'one child norm'.
steps: Strategy: motivate smaller families using contraceptive methods
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT says MTP is not meant for population control and condemns the misuse of amniocentesis for sex determination; ART is for infertile couples, not a population measure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): STIs in women may remain undetected or untreated for a long time.
Reason (R): In infected females, STIs are often asymptomatic, and the early symptoms of most STIs are minor.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: early symptoms of most of these diseases are minor, and these include itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings, etc., in the genital region. Infected females may often be asymptomatic and hence may remain undetected for long. Absent or less significant early symptoms (along with social stigma) deter people from timely detection and treatment. R gives the very reason for A.
steps: No or minor symptoms -> infection goes unnoticed -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT facts, so options with a false statement are wrong; NCERT links the absence of symptoms directly to infections remaining undetected, so R is the correct explanation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The chances of failure of periodic abstinence and coitus interruptus are high.
Statement II: Tubectomy is the sterilisation method adopted by the male partner.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: natural methods such as periodic abstinence and coitus interruptus have almost nil side effects, but their chances of failure are also high. Sterilisation in the male is called vasectomy (a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up); that in the female is called tubectomy (a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up).
steps: Statement II: false - tubectomy is for the female; vasectomy for the male
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II confuses tubectomy with vasectomy, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is NCERT's limitation of natural methods, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
